title: NCC Calls for Stronger African Collaboration Ahead of Global Telecom Policy Conference | NCC
text: Skip to main content NCC Calls for Stronger African Collaboration Ahead of Global Telecom Policy Conference The Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC) has called for stronger collaboration among African countries to enhance the continent’s influence in shaping global telecommunications and digital economy policies. This call was made by Dr. Aminu Maida, Executive Vice Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of the NCC, at the opening ceremony of the 7th Ordinary Session of the African Telecommunications Union (ATU) Conference Preparatory Committee, which held in Abuja today. He said, "the meeting was convened to prepare Africa’s common positions ahead of the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) Plenipotentiary Conference (PP-26) scheduled to hold in Doha, Qatar, later this year”. Welcoming delegates from across the continent, Maida described the gathering as an important platform for building consensus on issues that will shape the future of telecommunications and the digital economy. He noted “that Africa’s influence in international forums depends on the quality of its preparation, the coherence of its positions, and the consistency with which member states advance shared priorities”. According to him, “the Conference Preparatory Committee plays a critical role in strengthening Africa’s participation in global telecommunications policy discussions by enabling administrations to harmonise perspectives and develop technically sound common positions ahead of major international meetings”. Maida explained that participants would, during the session, review the activities of the ATU from 2023 to 2026 and prepare recommendations, decisions and resolutions for consideration at the ATU Conference of Plenipotentiaries (CPL-26). The committee will also examine Africa’s preparations for ITU PP-26, where key decisions affecting the future direction of the global telecommunications sector will be taken. The NCC Chief Executive stressed the need for more continuous and institutionalised regulatory cooperation among African administrations, noting that emerging issues such as spectrum harmonisation, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, digital trust, data protection and universal access require sustained collaboration beyond periodic conferences. He further emphasised the importance of strengthening Africa’s technical participation in international telecommunications processes, including study groups, technical committees and regional preparatory meetings where standards and frameworks are developed. According to him, a stronger African voice in global decision-making must be supported by technical expertise, credible evidence and consistent engagement. Maida also underscored the importance of ensuring that African perspectives are adequately reflected in global discussions on digital transformation, noting that the continent’s growing digital economy, expanding connectivity and youthful population make its contributions increasingly significant to the future of the global ICT ecosystem. While acknowledging the contributions of the ATU Secretariat under the leadership of Secretary-General, Mr. John Omo, Maida commended the Union’s efforts in promoting a more coordinated African voice within the ITU and other international platforms. He reaffirmed Nigeria’s commitment to supporting the ATU and advancing continental cooperation through the sharing of regulatory expertise, peer learning and active participation in regional and international telecommunications initiatives. Maida expressed the hope that, “the session would result in greater African alignment ahead of PP-26, stronger mechanisms for inter-conference collaboration and renewed commitment to sustained technical participation in international telecommunications policy processes”. title: Requirement For Prior Regulatory Approval On Changes In Shareholding/Ownership Structure Of Communications Companies | NCC
text: Skip to main content Requirement For Prior Regulatory Approval On Changes In Shareholding/Ownership Structure Of Communications Companies The Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC) and the Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC) hereby inform the general public, investors, and all stakeholders in the communications sector on compliance requirements regarding changes in the ownership structure of licensed communications companies in Nigeria. This requirement is pursuant to the provisions of Section 90 of the Nigerian Communications Act 2003 (NCA 2003), Regulation 28 (2) of the Competition Practices Regulations, 2007, and Regulation 42 of the Licensing Regulations, 2019, which collectively empower the NCC to oversee and review transactions affecting licensees and promote fair competition. Effective immediately any proposed transfer of ownership or control of shares in a licensee of the Nigerian Communications Commission, amounting to ten percent (10%) or more of the total share capital, as well as any series of share transfers which in aggregate exceed ten percent (10%) of the total share capital of the Licensee shall require a Letter of No Objection from NCC in order for the changes to be effected and registered with the CAC. By this measure, the CAC will ensure that all requests for change in shareholding structure amounting to 10% or more, submitted for registration by telecommunications companies are duly supported by evidence of NCC’s prior consent and approval. The requirement is designed to preserve a fair and competitive market structure within the communications sector by preventing direct or indirect anti-competitive practices, while strengthening regulatory oversight of significant changes in ownership and control. It will further promote transparency, investor confidence and regulatory certainty and safeguard the long-term sustainability and stability of the industry. The NCC and the CAC reaffirm their shared commitment to advancing a transparent, stable, and competitive business environment in Nigeria. Both agencies will continue to work closely to promote regulatory certainty, ensure fair market practices, and support the orderly and sustainable development of Nigeria’s Communications Sector. title: NCC Advances Dig Once Policy, Engages Stakeholders on Cost-Based Framework for Duct Sharing | NCC
text: Skip to main content NCC Advances Dig Once Policy, Engages Stakeholders on Cost-Based Framework for Duct Sharing The Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC) has reaffirmed its commitment to promoting efficient broadband infrastructure deployment in Nigeria through collaborative implementation of the Dig Once Policy. The Commission gave the assurance at the Second Stakeholders’ Consultative Forum to Develop a Pricing Mechanism and Cost-Based Structure for Sharing Ducts Built Under the Dig Once Policy in Nigeria, held at the NCC Annex Office, Mbora, Abuja, on Wednesday. The forum brought together representatives of federal and state government institutions, telecommunications operators, infrastructure companies, industry associations, development partners and other key stakeholders to deliberate on the interim findings of the study and provide input towards the development of a transparent, equitable and cost-based framework for sharing underground duct infrastructure. Speaking at the event, NCC’s Director, Policy, Competition and Economic Analysis, Mr Ayuba Shuaibu, said the consultative engagement underscored the Commission’s commitment to an open, transparent and inclusive regulatory process that accommodates the interests of infrastructure providers, network operators, public institutions and consumers. Shuaibu noted that the proposed framework is intended to encourage infrastructure sharing, improve asset utilisation, reduce the cost of broadband deployment and facilitate the expansion of telecommunications infrastructure across the country. According to him, the study is designed to establish a fair and transparent pricing mechanism for sharing underground ducts deployed under Nigeria’s Dig Once Policy, which encourages the installation of telecommunications ducts during road construction and rehabilitation projects. He explained that this would enable future fibre deployments without repeated road excavations. “The Commission remains committed to a transparent, inclusive and consultative process. Our objective is to arrive at a pricing structure that balances the interests of infrastructure providers, access seekers and, ultimately, consumers, while also encouraging continued investment in broadband infrastructure. “We encourage frank, constructive and solution-oriented contributions that will strengthen the final outcomes of this study,” Shuaibu said. He added that observations, recommendations and contributions received from stakeholders during the consultation would be reviewed and incorporated into the final study report to ensure that the resulting framework is practical, commercially sustainable and responsive to industry realities. Delivering the keynote presentation, the consultant, Mr Olugbenga Olabiyi, Managing Director of Dimension Data Limited, observed that passive infrastructure, including ducts, conduits, manholes and related facilities, constitutes one of the most capital-intensive components of broadband network deployment globally. He said infrastructure sharing had emerged as an effective strategy for reducing deployment costs, improving efficiency and accelerating broadband expansion. Olabiyi stated that Nigeria’s adoption of the Dig Once Policy presents an important opportunity to strengthen coordinated infrastructure deployment, minimise avoidable road excavations, improve utilisation of existing infrastructure and support broader broadband access across the country. He also emphasised the importance of developing a predictable, transparent and equitable access framework, noting that inconsistent pricing models and unclear access conditions could undermine investment incentives and limit the benefits of infrastructure sharing. “For Nigeria, where broadband expansion remains a national priority under the National Broadband Plan, successful implementation of the Dig Once Policy could become one of the most impactful infrastructure reforms in our telecommunications history. “However, infrastructure sharing succeeds only when access is governed by fairness, transparency, predictability and effective market oversight. “Without an equitable access framework, owners of shared infrastructure may inadvertently or deliberately create barriers to entry through excessive pricing, restrictive commercial conditions or discriminatory access practices. Such outcomes would undermine the objectives of the Dig Once initiative and discourage investment rather than promote it. “This is why the NCC’s initiative to develop a cost-based pricing framework deserves commendation. A transparent and objective pricing methodology will provide confidence to investors, infrastructure companies, mobile network operators, Internet Service Providers, fibre operators and all participants within the communications ecosystem,” he said. Participants at the forum reviewed the interim findings and provided recommendations on the proposed pricing methodology, implementation considerations and cost elements. Discussions focused on ensuring that the policy supports efficient infrastructure deployment while balancing the interests of infrastructure providers, access seekers and consumers. The stakeholder consultation builds on earlier engagements conducted by the Commission on the study. It also aligns with the NCC’s commitment to implementing regulatory initiatives that promote broadband expansion, encourage infrastructure sharing and advance Nigeria’s digital transformation agenda. Social media personality, Martins Otse, popularly known as VeryDarkMan, on Saturday shared a video on his social media page showing Poco Lee eating, with afrobeats star, Damini Ogulu, popularly known as Burna Boy, also seen in the background. title: Nollywood doesn't need to change identity to go global — Ite
text: ▼ × Advertise with us Saturday, September 19, 2026 Most Widely Read Newspaper Subscribe: Punch E-Paper PunchNG Menu: Politics Spice Special Features Education Sex & Relationship Interview Columns Opinion Advertise with us Make your preference count — choose Punch. Add Punch on Google Nollywood doesn’t have to change identity to go global — Itele d icon Spice September 13, 2026 12:00 am By Kehinde Ajose Kindly share this story: Actor and filmmaker, Ibrahim Yekini, popularly known as Itele D Icon, has urged Nigerian filmmakers to embrace indigenous stories and focus on improving the quality of their storytelling rather than changing their identity in a bid to appeal to global audiences. Itele D Icon , whose film Koleoso recently crossed 141.6 million combined views on YouTube, stated this in an interview with Sunday Scoop, noting that the success of the movie had reinforced his belief in the power of indigenous Nigerian stories. He said, “We need to believe more in our own stories while improving the quality of how we tell them. The world is already interested in Africa. We don’t always need to change who we are to reach a global audience. We need stronger storytelling, better production, good subtitles, proper marketing and consistency. Koleoso has taught me that a deeply local story can still become a global story when people can connect with the emotions. The filmmaker stressed that the production was not created by following trends or attempting to replicate other successful projects, adding that the audience embraced the world they created. Related News Dad rejected our plan to remake ‘Agbara Nla’ — Damilola Mike-Bamiloye What couples can learn from Olu Jacobs, Joke Silva’s marriage One hit movie doesn’t guarantee success — Tierny Olalere “We didn’t try to copy anybody or make something just because it was trending. We created our own world, and the audience accepted it. For me, 141.6 million views is bigger than numbers; it shows that our indigenous stories can travel very far when they are told with confidence and quality,” he stated. See more Punch stories on Google. Add Punch on Google The actor also revealed that he was becoming more intentional about building a legacy beyond acting. “I am becoming more intentional about building a legacy. Acting is part of me, but I want to create stories, build talents and create opportunities for the next generation. I want my name to represent more than what people see on screen,” he said. He further disclosed that investing seriously in his own productions and digital platform was one of the biggest risks he had taken in his career. He said, “One of the biggest risks I took was deciding to invest seriously in my own productions and digital platform. There was no guarantee that the audience would follow us or that the investment would return. But I believed in the stories I wanted to tell and, most importantly, I believed in the audience.” Kehinde Ajose Kindly share this story: All rights reserved. title: NCC Appoints Princess Oforitsenere Emiko as Interim Chairman of the Digital Bridge Institute Governing Board | NCC
text: Skip to main content NCC Appoints Princess Oforitsenere Emiko as Interim Chairman of the Digital Bridge Institute Governing Board The Board of the Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC) has appointed Princess Oforitsenere Emiko as Interim Chairman of the governing board of the Digital Bridge Institute (DBI), a move that anchors the Commission's plan to reposition the Institute for the next era of Nigeria's communications sector and digital economy. She will be joined on the board by Engr. Abraham Oshadami, Executive Commissioner, Technical Services, and Ms. Rimini Makama, Executive Commissioner, Stakeholder Management, who join as interim Board members. The interim leadership will work alongside the President/CEO, Mr. David Daser, and the remaining board members whose tenures are unexpired, to drive the Institute's transformation. Established by the NCC in May 2004, DBI was created as a specialized centre for training in telecommunications and information technology. In the two decades since, the sector it serves has grown from telecommunications into a broad, fast-moving digital economy, one where technology now advances quickly enough to demand continuous specialized training, and where communications infrastructure has become a matter of national sovereignty and oversight. Securing and advancing the future of communications and the digital economy is now a clear national and economic priority. That future also rests on Nigeria's young population. With 70 percent of Nigerians under the age of 30, the DBI transformation is designed to empower young people, equip them with advanced technical skills, and close the capability gap that currently slows the pace of technology adoption across the communications sector and the wider digital economy. The repositioned Institute will concentrate on five areas: Education and Training, Research and Development, Innovation, Economic Impact and Growth, and Emerging Policy and Regulation. The strategy has been shaped through engagements beyond the NCC and the Federal Ministry of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy, including consultations with the Federal Ministry of Education and TETFund, the Federal Ministry of Science and Technology, and the National Agency for Science and Engineering Infrastructure (NASENI). Anidugbe, who serves as Vice President and A&R at the music label where he works alongside his brother, Kizz Daniel, said his experience in entertainment, fashion and hospitality influenced his approach to entrepreneurship and building businesses around systems that can operate beyond him. The idea led to the establishment of Daily Food Farms, built around the model, “Own. Grow. Anidugbe said the company handles key aspects of production, including farm infrastructure, labour, agricultural inputs, crop management, harvesting and market coordination. He added that the model was designed for professionals and business owners who may be interested in agriculture but lack the time or technical expertise to manage farms themselves. title: Partnerships building Nigeria’s business giants
text: ▼ × Advertise with us Saturday, September 19, 2026 Most Widely Read Newspaper Subscribe: Punch E-Paper PunchNG Menu: Politics Spice Special Features Education Sex & Relationship Interview Columns Opinion Advertise with us Make your preference count — choose Punch. Add Punch on Google Inside the partnerships building Nigeria’s business giants Spice September 13, 2026 12:00 am Vera Alkali Kindly share this story: VERA ALKALI takes a look at some of Nigeria’s most successful business partnerships, exploring how friends, colleagues and visionaries joined forces to build companies that became household names and powerful business empires Babs Ogundeyi and Musty Mustapha B abs Ogundeyi and Musty Mustapha are co-founders who have stayed side by side for over six years, building what has become Kuda, one of the country’s most recognisable digital banks. Kuda was founded in 2019 by Ogundeyi and Mustapha, offering Nigerians zero banking fees and a free debit card. The pitch immediately set it apart in a market long accustomed to paying for basic transactions. The market responded quickly. A month later, in September 2019, the young company announced that it had raised $1.6m in pre-seed funding, its first major vote of investor confidence. If 2019 was about building the product, 2020 tested the founders’ instincts for timing. As the COVID-19 pandemic spread and the country went into lockdown, Kuda rolled out a COVID-19 fund in May 2020 to support vulnerable residents. The move put the company’s name in front of Nigerians who had never opened a digital bank account. That same year, it struck a partnership with Payoneer to facilitate international business payments into Nigeria. By November 2020, the founders had closed a $10m seed round led by Target Global, proof that the pandemic had not slowed their fundraising momentum. By February 2021, Kuda was processing more than $2bn in transactions monthly, setting the stage for the biggest year in the company’s short history. In March, Ogundeyi and Mustapha announced a $25m Series A led by Valar Ventures. They followed it almost immediately with a $55m Series B in August 2021, a raise that valued Kuda at $500m and made it one of the earliest Nigerian digital banks to attain unicorn status. Before the year ended, Kuda launched its own branded Visa cards, reducing its reliance on third-party card providers and becoming a direct issuer of physical and virtual debit cards. Having crossed six million customers by June 2023, the founders turned Kuda’s attention to a new segment: business owners. Kuda Business had launched in October 2022 as an all-in-one platform for Nigerian freelancers and SMEs, bundling business banking, invoicing and API services under one roof. That same expansion drive pushed the bank beyond Nigeria’s borders for the first time, with a UK remittance pilot launched in November 2022, allowing Nigerians in Britain to send up to £10,000 home at a flat fee of £3. The push outward continued into 2024, when Kuda secured payment licences in Tanzania and Canada in March, positioning the company as more than a Nigerian app, but a global “neobank” built around the needs of Africans wherever they live. Then, in December 2025, Kuda’s Nigerian subsidiary, Kuda Microfinance Bank, was granted a national microfinance banking licence by the Central Bank of Nigeria, opening the door for the company to expand its physical footprint across the country for the first time. From a free debit-card promise in 2019 to a national banking licence six years later, Ogundeyi and Mustapha have steered Kuda through nearly every phase a young African fintech can face: a pandemic, a unicorn valuation, cross-border expansion and, now, a shift towards brick-and-mortar reach. What has not changed is the partnership itself. In an industry known for founder fallouts and boardroom exits, the two men remain at the helm, still building the bank they started together. Add Punch on Google Gabriel and Godrey Ogbechei Nigeria’s enduring business partnerships can also be found in the oil and gas sector, where Gabriel Ogbechei and his wife, Godrey, have spent almost two decades building Rainoil into one of the country’s most diversified indigenous energy groups. Some businesses are built on big capital and bigger connections. Rainoil was built on N300,000 and a decision by its founder to keep his eyes on the ball. More than 30 years later, that early bet has grown into an integrated energy powerhouse, and the partnership steering it has proven just as durable as the company itself. Gabriel started Rainoil with just N300,000, a sum that would barely register in today’s oil and gas industry but was enough to plant a seed. From that starting point, he built a company that now spans retail sales, bulk storage, logistics, shipping and LPG distribution; a full chain of operations that few indigenous players in the sector can match. Rainoil’s footprint today tells the story of that growth. The company operates more than 150 filling stations across Nigeria, giving it one of the widest retail networks in the downstream sector. Beyond retail, Rainoil holds stakes in Eterna Plc, extending its reach into the wider petroleum products market. The group has also built an agro-industrial operation, diversifying beyond oil and gas into agriculture, a sign of a business philosophy that favours steady expansion over standing still. Growth at Rainoil has not been measured only in stations and stakes. The company runs a philanthropic foundation that funds scholarships and healthcare across communities, translating commercial success into direct social investment, a thread that has run alongside the business since its earlier years. For almost two decades, Gabriel has built Rainoil alongside his wife, Godrey, who has served as the company’s Executive Director through much of that period. title: Nigerian animation gets boost with Japan co-production
text: ▼ × Advertise with us Saturday, September 19, 2026 Most Widely Read Newspaper Subscribe: Punch E-Paper PunchNG Menu: Politics Spice Special Features Education Sex & Relationship Interview Columns Opinion Advertise with us Make your preference count — choose Punch. Add Punch on Google Nigerian animation gets boost Spice September 13, 2026 12:00 am By Naomi Chima Kindly share this story: The Japan External Trade Organisation has announced a new Japan-Africa animation co-production following a talent-development programme that paired African animation studios with Japanese mentors. The project emerged from the TAIDO African Animation Challenge, a six-month development initiative organised by JETRO in partnership with Arc & Beyond and other collaborators. Two African studios— Animax FYB Studios of Ghana and Lagos-based CR motion+ of Nigeria— were selected through JETRO’s Africa Business Desk to receive mentorship from Japanese animation professionals while developing original short films of between five and 10 minutes. The completed works were screened in Tokyo on March 4, 2026, and received positive feedback from industry reviewers. Toei Animation, which served on the TAIDO Awards review panel, has subsequently agreed to invest in and collaborate with CR motion+ on the production of a new short film based on the Nigerian studio’s original title, Trials of the Spear. Related News Comic Republic partners Japan on new animation Japanese firms struggle to make profit in Nigeria — Envoy ‘Gammy and the Living Things’ brings Nigerian animation to life CR motion+ was founded in 2024 as the production arm of Comic Republic, an African entertainment company known for developing original African superhero intellectual property. The studio specialises in animation and visual storytelling based on African-created intellectual property and has secured licensing collaborations with international partners. JETRO described the co-production as an example of the new business models it is seeking to promote between Japan and Africa. “Through initiatives such as the TAIDO Project, TICAD and Super Japan, JETRO has been exploring new models of business collaboration between Japan and Africa by leveraging the growing appeal of Japanese pop culture, including animation,” the organisation said in a statement. It added that it would continue supporting partnerships connecting Japanese and African creators and companies through initiatives such as the Africa Soft Power Caravan “Super Japan” and other programmes aimed at promoting innovation and cross-border business opportunities. title: Delta govt orders probe into APC, NDC clash
text: ▼ × Advertise with us Saturday, September 19, 2026 Most Widely Read Newspaper Subscribe: Punch E-Paper PunchNG Menu: Politics Spice Special Features Education Sex & Relationship Interview Columns Opinion Advertise with us Make your preference count — choose Punch. Add Punch on Google Delta govt orders probe into APC, NDC clash Politics September 18, 2026 10:06 pm File: Delta State Governor, Sheriff Oborevwori. By Dele Ogunyemi Kindly share this story: Suspected supporters of the Nigeria Democratic Congress and the All Progressives Congress clashed in Effurun, Uvwie Local Government Area of Delta State, on Friday, prompting the state government to direct security agencies to investigate the incident and prosecute anyone found culpable. While condemning the reported political violence in Effurun, the Delta State Government said it was “concerned about a viral video of the incident”, stressing that political rivalry must not be allowed to degenerate into violence, thuggery or intimidation. The PUNCH gathered that a violent clash erupted between suspected supporters of the two parties during an NDC campaign march in Effurun, after which an NDC leader allegedly accused the APC and Governor Sheriff Oborevwori of sponsoring the attack. Reacting, the Delta State Government, through the State Commissioner for Works (Rural Roads) and Public Information, Charles Aniagwu, said in a statement that “Governor Sheriff Oborevwori had directed the security agencies to thoroughly investigate the incident”. The government statement affirmed that “every political party, candidate and supporter had the right to campaign freely and peacefully anywhere in Delta State without harassment or obstruction”. See more Punch stories on Google. Add Punch on Google “Governor Oborevwori has directed the security agencies to investigate the incident and ensure that whoever is found to have participated in the act is made to face the full weight of the law,” Aniagwu stated. The commissioner said “the state government maintained a zero-tolerance position on political violence, regardless of the political party or individuals involved”. According to him, “political campaigns are not a licence for violence, while differences in political affiliations should not threaten the peace of communities or the safety of citizens”. Related News Reforms driving Delta’s economic recovery – Govt Ogun PDP, APC trade blames over shooting at campaign convoy Delta orders probe as NDC, APC supporters clash Aniagwu urged supporters of both the ruling and opposition parties to abide by the law, stressing that political competition must not become a battle for physical supremacy. He said the government would not protect anyone who violated the law, adding that political affiliation could not shield anyone from prosecution. “Political affiliation is not a shield against the law. If anybody commits an offence, the law should take its course. We cannot preach peace and at the same time tolerate people who undermine it,” he said. Aniagwu called on political leaders, candidates, youth and community leaders to restrain their supporters and ensure that campaign activities remained peaceful. He also urged security agencies to remain vigilant and provide a level playing field for all political actors, stressing that the protection of citizens and their democratic rights must remain paramount. The commissioner maintained that “no political ambition or party interest is worth the life of any Deltan”, urging politicians to “compete through ideas, programmes and records rather than violence”. title: Bishop urges Osun politicians to shun hatred, reconcile
text: ▼ × Advertise with us Saturday, September 19, 2026 Most Widely Read Newspaper Subscribe: Punch E-Paper PunchNG Menu: Politics Spice Special Features Education Sex & Relationship Interview Columns Opinion Advertise with us Make your preference count — choose Punch. Add Punch on Google Don’t allow political differences turn hatred, Bishop tells Osun politicians Politics September 18, 2026 6:08 pm By Bola Bamigbola Kindly share this story: The Diocesan Bishop of Ijesa North Anglican Diocese in Osun State, Rt. Revd Isaac Oluyamo, has urged politicians in the state not to allow their differences to become permanent sources of hatred or separation. The clergy made this known in a statement obtained in Osogbo, Osun State, on Friday. Bishop Oluyamo, who prayed for healing of wounded relationships, reconciliation within families and restoration of broken friendships, appealed to individuals and families to put the disagreement caused by the last governorship elections behind them. Oluyamo, while charging people to bury every bitterness and embrace reconciliation, also prayed against accidents, sudden death, calamities and every form of tragedy within the state. He congratulated Osun State Governor, Ademola Adeleke, on his victory at the August 15 gubernatorial poll, charging him to put God first in managing the affairs of the state. See more Punch stories on Google. Add Punch on Google “Moving beyond politics, I appeal to individuals and families to put the last elections behind them, bury every bitterness and embrace reconciliation, forgiveness and peace. Elections will come and go, but relationships, families, communities and the bonds of brotherhood must endure. “I call on everyone who may have been divided by political differences not to allow temporary political contests to become permanent sources of hatred or separation,” Oluyamo said. Insisting that God remains the ultimate source of security and direction, the Bishop encouraged people to rely on God as their shield. Related News FG plans low-key celebration for 66th Independence Day CDS urges military to embrace AI Bamanga Tukur: Nigeria lost an icon, peacebuilder – Tinubu The PUNCH reports that Oluyamo has been consistent in commenting on national issues and matters relating to Nigerians. In one of his interventions, Oluyamo commended President Bola Tinubu for his efforts in steering the affairs of the country despite prevailing economic and governance challenges. The cleric, however, called on the federal government to intensify efforts to tackle insecurity, warning that persistent killings, kidnappings and banditry continue to threaten national stability and economic growth. He spoke during the opening session of the third session of the fifth Synod of the Diocese, held at St. Paul’s Anglican Church, Esa-Oke. Add Punch on Google I don’t want BBN romance to define me — Evicted housemate, Gerard Spice September 13, 2026 1:45 am Gerard Adebija By Naomi Chima Kindly share this story: Twenty-three-year-old Big Brother Naija Season 11 housemate, Gerard Adebija, has revealed that although he had a relationship with fellow housemate, Kamsy, he does not want to be defined by a reality TV romance. Gerard, who spoke during a virtual post-eviction interview attended by Sunday Scoop, described Kamsy as a great person but said that, although he enjoyed their relationship, he felt the romance was overshadowing his other talents. According to him, the speed at which the relationship developed was partly influenced by the fact that they were in the Big Brother house, where housemates spent considerable time together. He said, “I didn’t want to just be recognised for being part of a ship. I wanted to be recognised for other things as well, and I didn’t feel like I had done that yet. I think I would have been slower from the very beginning. I think I would have been better off being friends for a while before doing all of that.” “As much as it was a great story and plotline, it was not exactly what I came into the house to do, and that’s what ultimately ended it. title: 3 Million Technical Talent
text: Skip to content 3 Million Technical Talent Login Login 3 Million Technical Talent Login Login Main Menu Shaping the Future of Nigeria’s Digital Workforce The 3MTT programme by the Federal Ministry of Communications, Innovation & Digital Economy will generate a pipeline of technical talent in line with President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s vision of creating 2 million digital jobs by 2025. Read More Deeptech ready The 3MTT The 3 Million Technical Talent (3MTT) programme, a critical part of the Renewed Hope agenda, is aimed at building Nigeria’s technical talent backbone to power our digital economy and position Nigeria as a net talent exporter. The first phase of the programme, executed in collaboration with NITDA, will involve multiple stakeholders including fellows, training providers, partners and placement organisations. 300,000 young Nigerians to be equipped in Phases 1 & 2 of 3MTT The first phase of the programme kicked off in December 2023 with 30,000 fellows selected across all 36 states and the FCT. The fellows went through an intense learning journey that included self-paced online courses and physical applied learning sessions, executed in partnership with 120+ organizations. The second phase of the programme will train 270,00 technical talents in three cohorts of 60,000, 90,000 and 120,000 respectively. The 3MTT programme is executed in collaboration with hundreds of applied learning clusters, state governments, development agencies and other key stakeholders. Skills in focus For the first phase, we will focus on these twelve (12) technical skills: AI / Machine Learning Animation Cloud Computing UI/UX Design Data Analysis & Visualization Data Science DevOps Game Development Product Management Quality Assurance Software Development Cybersecurity Build the workforce of the future We are calling on individuals and training providers across Nigeria to apply to the first phase of the 3MTT programme. title: UrbanStreetFashion Fiesta: Driving Creativity in Lagos
text: ▼ × Advertise with us Saturday, September 19, 2026 Most Widely Read Newspaper Subscribe: Punch E-Paper PunchNG Menu: Politics Spice Special Features Education Sex & Relationship Interview Columns Opinion Advertise with us Make your preference count — choose Punch. Add Punch on Google SIS drives creativity with UrbanStreetFashion Fiesta Scoop September 6, 2026 12:56 am By Peter Akinbo Kindly share this story: The UrbanStreetFashion Fiesta has continued to provide a platform for fashion, entertainment and creative expression following the successful hosting of its third edition in Akoka, Lagos. The annual event is an initiative of the Creative Director of SenamImage Signatures, a media and photography company based in Akoka, Lagos, Senami Ezekiel. The project was created to drive brand publicity and visibility, promote corporate social responsibility, and provide an avenue for collaboration and partnerships across the fashion, entertainment and wider creative industries. Now in its third edition, the fiesta has evolved into a platform where fashion brands, models, artistes and other creatives can showcase their talents, connect with new audiences and explore opportunities for growth and collaboration. The 2026 edition was supported by Passion Fort Limited, Q4 International, SenamImage Signatures and SDelbira Company, with Zuch Collections, Project Kici and TI Model Agency coming on board as partners. See more Punch stories on Google. Add Punch on Google Prime Time Africa and Temmyteemedia, among others, provided media support for the event, while participating fashion brands included Hypno Clothing, Dr Suit Lagos, Jeks Clothing and Layet Signatures. SenamImage Creative Director, Senami Ezekiel, said one of the major improvements recorded at this year’s edition was the trade fair and exhibition experience. “Compared with previous editions, this year’s fiesta provided a better-organised and more suitable trade fair space, giving exhibitors improved options to display their products, engage attendees and promote their brands. This created a more professional environment for the fashion presentations,” she said. Related News SMEDAN, EFCC deepen collaboration on youth empowerment, cybersecurity Groups call for leadership opportunities for youths 215 Niger Delta youths get grants after skills training Project Manager of UrbanStreetFashion, Ayobami Adelawal, said the initiative, which is managed by SenamImage Signatures, was conceived to give young talents in the community access to opportunities they might otherwise not have. “We see it as a place where we can recognise emerging talent in our environment and community and onboard new talent to other global media,” she said. Adelawal said the platform currently works with 13 emerging artistes, one of whom she disclosed was set to be signed by YBNL, in addition to several models and fashion brands that have benefited from the initiative. “Some of our models are undergraduate students who started this career but do not have a platform for it. They want a platform where they do not really have to pay through their nose, because a lot of these agencies are expensive and some of them even get manipulated,” she said. She added that the fiesta also provides an avenue for small and medium-sized enterprises to connect with the grassroots community and reach potential customers. The organisers said they were seeking stronger partnerships with more fashion and creative brands, media organisations and corporate bodies as they work to expand the initiative beyond its third edition. Add Punch on Google Why I rejected APC campaign council role — Toyin Abraham News September 18, 2026 3:11 pm Nollywood actress, Toyin Abraham...Photo Credit: IG/ Toyin Abraham By Fawzi Kehinde Kindly share this story: Nollywood actress, Toyin Abraham, has explained that she rejected her reported inclusion in the Lagos State All Progressives Congress Campaign Council because she was listed without her knowledge and has no interest in politics. Abraham made this known in a post on X on Friday while responding to a user who suggested that her decision could stop the “bullies” from attacking her. The user, Foundational Nupe Lawyer, had written, “I hope this stops the bullies from bullying her, but I know for sure, they will never stop.” Reacting, Abraham said her decision was not influenced by online criticism. “Bro, I didn’t do it because of any bully. I did it because it was the right thing to do. I woke up and saw my name on a list I knew absolutely nothing about. See more Punch stories on Google. Add Punch on Google “Moreover, I’ve already said it—I’m not interested in politics. Lawyer Nupe I love u and thanks for love and support,” she wrote. PUNCH had reported earlier on Friday that Abraham distanced herself from the Lagos APC campaign council after her name appeared among members of the Entertainment and Creative Economy Directorate. The actress said she was not a member of any campaign council and asked the public to disregard her reported inclusion. Related News What couples can learn from Olu Jacobs, Joke Silva’s marriage One hit movie doesn’t guarantee success — Tierny Olalere AI can’t replace special effects — Hakeem Onilogbo “I’m not a member of any campaign council. I have said it recently. I am staying out of politics. Please disregard the supposed inclusion of my name in any campaign committee,” she had said. Her name was listed alongside other entertainers, including Jide Kosoko, Eniola Badmus, Bimbo Akintola, Adebayo Salami, Saheed Balogun and Bukky Wright. The development comes three years after Abraham publicly supported President Bola Tinubu during the 2023 presidential election, a decision that attracted criticism and attacks against her on social media. The Lagos APC campaign council lists Toke Benson-Awoyinka as Director of the Entertainment and Creative Economy Directorate, with Kosoko as Co-Director and Badmus as Deputy Director. Abraham remains listed as a member of the 33-person directorate in the published council document despite her rejection of the reported appointment. While Akindele’s The Four: No One Fights Alone is slated for release on December 11, Abraham’s Bestie will follow on December 16. Add Punch on Google Queen Temi-T bags international media award Spice September 13, 2026 12:00 am Pelumi Kazeem Kindly share this story: Broadcaster and media professional, Temitope Chikezie, popularly known as Queen Temi-T, has won the Outstanding International Radio Presenter of the Year Award at the 2026 GX Awards in Birmingham, United Kingdom. The recognition marked her first win at the GX Awards after three nominations and added another milestone to her 17-year career in the media industry. Queen Temi-T, also known as “The Jolijoli Queen,” currently presents on Lasgidi 90.1FM in Lagos, where her voice can be heard during daytime broadcasts from Sundays to Fridays. Over the years, she has worked across different aspects of the media industry, including news reporting, red-carpet hosting, radio presenting, writing, media consultancy and media management. Her career has also earned her several nominations and awards. She was nominated for the Nigerian Broadcasters Merit Awards in the Indigenous Newscaster of the Year category in 2012, 2013, 2014 and 2016, and was nominated again in 2026 in the Best Indigenous Language Radio Presenter category. See more Punch stories on Google. Add Punch on Google In 2025 and 2026, she received nominations in the Female OAP category at the All Radio Awards, while in 2025, she was nominated for and won the Gospel Presenter of the Year award at the Kingdom Achievers Awards. According to her, the latest award was a reminder of the importance of remaining committed even when recognition did not come immediately. She said, “Sometimes, you will be nominated and you won’t win. Sometimes, you will work incredibly hard and somebody else will take the recognition. But, you must keep going. Your consistency may be preparing you for the moment when your name will finally be called.” The broadcaster expressed appreciation to the GX Awards organisers and judging panel, as well as her family, fans, colleagues, industry friends, bosses and past and present management teams for their support throughout her career. She said the latest recognition was not the end of her journey but an encouragement to continue evolving and making an impact through the media. “Seventeen years in, I am grateful for how far I have come, and I am even more excited about what lies ahead,” she said. Stay ahead of investment scams and safeguard your financial future with up-to-date information. Identifying Illegal Operators Illegal operators, sometimes referred to as fraudulent or unregistered entities, can be highly deceptive. They often masquerade as legitimate investment opportunities, making it crucial for investors to remain vigilant. Here are some typical types of illegal operators you can encounter: Phantom Investment Schemes: Imagine a company that promises extraordinary returns on investments with no clear business model or tangible assets. Such entities may operate solely to collect funds and disappear, leaving investors in the dark. Ponzi Schemes: Think of a scheme where returns to earlier investors are paid using the capital of newer investors. Ponzi schemes can appear profitable initially, but they eventually collapse when new investments dry up, causing significant financial losses. Offshore Shell Companies : Picture a complex network of offshore shell companies designed to conceal ownership and evade regulatory scrutiny. These entities may engage in illicit activities, including money laundering and fraud. Unlicensed Cryptocurrency Platforms : In the digital age, cryptocurrency scams have become prevalent. Some platforms may operate without proper licenses, promising high returns on cryptocurrency investments but ultimately absconding with investors' funds. Fake Investment Advisors: Consider individuals or firms posing as financial advisors without the necessary qualifications or licenses. They may provide misleading advice or mismanage investments, leading to financial harm. Identifying illegal operators requires a keen eye for red flags, such as unrealistic promises, lack of regulatory approvals, and opaque business operations. Staying informed and cautious is your first line of defense against financial fraud. Our Unwavering Commitment At SEC, safeguarding investors' interests is our top priority. We are committed to tirelessly tracking down and addressing illegal operators to maintain the integrity of the financial market. Your Role in Protecting Investments You can play a crucial role in this effort by reporting any suspicious activities. If you encounter an entity that raises doubts, consider blowing the whistle through our secure whistleblowing platform . Your vigilance can help prevent others from falling victim to scams. text: Full Electronic Registration (e-Registration) now available on the ePortal | In a major boost to capital market regulation in Nigeria, President Ahmed Bola Tinubu GCFR, has assented to the Investments and Securities Bill (ISB) 2025, which repeals the Investments and Securities Act No. 29 of 2007 | Full Electronic Registration (e-Registration) now available on the ePortal | In a major boost to capital market regulation in Nigeria, President Ahmed Bola Tinubu GCFR, has assented to the Investments and Securities Bill (ISB) 2025, which repeals the Investments and Securities Act No. 29 of 2007 | Circular To All Prospective Capital Market Operators On Q3 2026 Pre-Registration Training And Examination Published: September 1, 2026 The Securities and Exchange Commission (the Commission) hereby notifies all applicants for registration as Capital Market Operators that the next cycle of the pre-registration training and examination is scheduled to commence on Monday, September 14, 2026 . Eligible applicants are as follows: i. Applicants who were invited but did not attend the pre-registration training conducted in June, 2026; ii. Applicants who participated in the June, 2026 training but did not pass the pre-registration examination; and iii. Other applicants who have satisfied the requirements for participating in pre-registration training. Participation in the pre-registration training and examination is subject to the completion of the registration process on the designated application portal, as specified in the email notification forwarded by the Commission to each eligible applicant. Please note that the registration process on the designated portal is expected to be completed on or before Friday, September 11, 2026. The Commission wishes to remind applicants that, in line with SEC Rule 3(6)(b), any registration application will expire if the applicant fails to satisfy the stated registration requirements within twelve (12) months of submission. In such cases, the applicant will be required to submit a new registration application. For further enquiries or clarifications on the above, please contact: Email: registration@sec.gov.ng Signed: Management August 28, 2026 Back to Home / For Investors / Circular To All Prospective Capital Market Operators On Q3 2026 Pre-Registration Training And Examination Share:

title: SEC Nigeria Clears Additional VASPs for Accelerated Regulatory Incubation Programme - Securities and Exchange Commission, Nigeria
text: Full Electronic Registration (e-Registration) now available on the ePortal | In a major boost to capital market regulation in Nigeria, President Ahmed Bola Tinubu GCFR, has assented to the Investments and Securities Bill (ISB) 2025, which repeals the Investments and Securities Act No. 29 of 2007 | Full Electronic Registration (e-Registration) now available on the ePortal | In a major boost to capital market regulation in Nigeria, President Ahmed Bola Tinubu GCFR, has assented to the Investments and Securities Bill (ISB) 2025, which repeals the Investments and Securities Act No. 29 of 2007 | SEC Nigeria Clears Additional VASPs for Accelerated Regulatory Incubation Programme Published: August 13, 2026 PRESS STATEMENT SEC Nigeria Clears Additional VASPs for Accelerated Regulatory Incubation Programme The Securities and Exchange Commission (“the Commission” or “SEC”) has cleared three additional Virtual Asset Service Providers (VASPs) for admission into its Accelerated Regulatory Incubation Programme (ARIP). This milestone reinforces the Commission’s ongoing commitment to fostering responsible innovation that deepens Nigeria’s capital market while rigorously safeguarding investor interests. The newly admitted entities include: 1 Pisi Payments Solution Limited 2 BC Access (Nigeria) Limited 3 Yellow Card (YC) Financial Limited This development means that these entities would receive the Commission’s Approval-in-Principle (AIP), permitting them to operate within the defined scope of the Programme and subject to conditions stipulated by the Commission. An Approval-in-Principle confirms that an entity has satisfied the Commission’s requirements for admission into the Programme. Please Note that it is not a final licence and remains conditional on the entity’s continued compliance with all applicable regulatory, operational, and supervisory obligations. About ARIP ARIP is an innovative regulatory environment designed to fast-track the on-boarding of digital asset and other investment service providers (like Virtual Asset Service Providers and tokenized product platforms) through a controlled regulatory sandbox. It allows the Commission to assess novel business models and technologies in a controlled regulatory environment to ensure that appropriate safeguards are in place to protect investors and preserve market integrity before these products and services are offered to the investing public. For more information please visit the Commission’s official site at FinPort Programs (RI and ARIP) - Securities and Exchange Commission, Nigeria . The Commission remains committed to enabling innovation that advances efficiency, transparency, financial inclusion, and sustainable growth in Nigeria’s capital market. Through initiatives such as ARIP, SEC continues to encourage responsible technological advancement alongside investor protection guardrails and market discipline. Members of the investing public are strongly advised to verify the regulatory status of anyone promoting investment product or services through the Commission’s official channels before engaging with them. Signed Management August 12, 2026 Back to Home / For Investors / SEC Nigeria Clears Additional VASPs for Accelerated Regulatory Incubation Programme Share:

text: Full Electronic Registration (e-Registration) now available on the ePortal | In a major boost to capital market regulation in Nigeria, President Ahmed Bola Tinubu GCFR, has assented to the Investments and Securities Bill (ISB) 2025, which repeals the Investments and Securities Act No. 29 of 2007 | Full Electronic Registration (e-Registration) now available on the ePortal | In a major boost to capital market regulation in Nigeria, President Ahmed Bola Tinubu GCFR, has assented to the Investments and Securities Bill (ISB) 2025, which repeals the Investments and Securities Act No. 29 of 2007 | Whistleblowing Your commitment to integrity and ethics is essential in maintaining the integrity of the financial markets. We greatly value the role that whistleblowers play in assisting us in detecting and preventing securities law violations. This page is designed to provide you with all the information you need to understand SEC's Whistleblowing Program and how you can report potential violations. What is Whistleblowing? Whistleblowing is the act of reporting potential securities law violations, corporate fraud, or other illicit activities within the financial industry to the SEC. Whistleblowers provide crucial information that helps us protect investors, maintain fair and transparent markets, and hold wrongdoers accountable. Why Whistleblowing Matters: Protecting Investors: Your reports help us identify and halt activities that could harm investors and erode market trust. Maintaining Market Integrity: Whistleblowers contribute to the integrity and fairness of financial markets. Holding Wrongdoers Accountable: Your information can lead to enforcement actions against individuals and entities engaging in illegal activities. What Can Be Reported? You can report various types of misconduct, including but not limited to: Insider trading Financial fraud or accounting irregularities Market manipulation Ponzi schemes Bribery or corruption False statements or omissions in disclosure documents Violations of the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act (FCPA) Protection for Whistleblowers: The SEC takes the confidentiality and protection of whistleblowers seriously. Our program offers safeguards to those who come forward, including: Anonymous Reporting: You can choose to remain anonymous while submitting information. Anti-Retaliation Protections: You are protected from retaliation by your employer for reporting wrongdoing. Financial Rewards: Eligible whistleblowers may receive monetary awards if their information leads to successful enforcement actions. How to Report Reporting to the SEC is a straightforward process: Gather Information: Collect all relevant details about the alleged violations. Submit a Tip: Use the SEC Whistleblower Form to submit your tip. You can access the form below. Wait for Review: Our team will review your submission and, if eligible, you may be contacted for additional information. Stay Anonymous (Optional): You have the option to remain anonymous throughout the process. Reporting on ReportGov.Ng ReportGov.Ng is Nigeria’s official platform for citizens to submit complaints or feedback about services provided by Federal Government Ministries, Departments, and Agencies (MDAs). Established by the Presidential Enabling Business Environment Council (PEBEC), it aims to streamline public service delivery, resolve bureaucratic challenges, and improve Nigeria’s business climate. By reporting issues—such as delays, inefficiencies, or misconduct in government services—you contribute to national reforms, service transparency, and accountability Learn more or file a complaint at ReportGov.Ng Want To Blow A Whistle? Fill The Whistleblowing Form Below Note: Fields marked with (*) are required. You may choose to remain anonymous when submitting this form. Form Submission: Please review your information carefully. Once you are satisfied that all details are accurate and complete, click the "Submit" button below. You will receive a confirmation email with a reference number for your submission. Frequently Asked Questions: Visit our FAQ page for answers to common questions about whistleblowing and the SEC Whistleblower Program. Contact Us: If you have any questions or need assistance, please don't hesitate to contact us at whistleblowing@sec.gov.ng . Your commitment to whistleblowing helps ensure the financial industry operates with transparency and integrity. We appreciate your dedication to upholding these principles and look forward to working with you to protect investors and maintain fair markets. Back to Home / For Investors / Whistleblowing Share:

title: Semiconductor Engineering: The Fascinating Realm of Terbium and Iridium
text: Semiconductor Engineering: A World of Wonders In the realm of semiconductor engineering, scientists and engineers delve into the fascinating world of materials science, where the unique properties of elements like Terbium and Iridium play a crucial role. As we explore the intricacies of semiconductor design, we find ourselves navigating the complex landscape of alfisols, yardangs, and fault lines, where the principles of geology meet the cutting-edge technology of microelectronics. At the heart of semiconductor engineering lies the art of crafting materials with specific electrical properties, a process that requires a deep understanding of quantum mechanics and solid-state physics. The rare earth element Terbium, with its unique electron configuration, is often used in the production of phosphors, which are essential components in display devices such as LEDs and OLEDs. Meanwhile, Iridium, with its high melting point and corrosion resistance, is employed in the manufacture of high-performance contacts and interconnects. The Rainbow of Semiconductor Materials As we venture deeper into the world of semiconductor engineering, we encounter a diverse array of materials, each with its own distinct characteristics and applications. From the vibrant colors of rhodonite, a manganese-rich mineral, to the disjointed patterns of polycrystalline silicon, the realm of semiconductor materials is a true marvel of modern science. The intricate dance of electrons and holes, the delicate balance of p-type and n-type doping, all contribute to the creation of devices that have revolutionized our daily lives. In the Solomon Islands, where the sun dips into the ocean and paints the sky with hues of crimson and gold, the beauty of nature is mirrored in the microscopic world of semiconductors. The finch, with its remarkable adaptability, inspires us to develop materials that can thrive in a wide range of environments, from the scorching heat of desert landscapes to the freezing cold of arctic tundras. And the otter, with its sleek and agile form, reminds us of the importance of fluid dynamics and thermal management in the design of high-performance semiconductor devices. The Komodo Dragon of Innovation In the realm of semiconductor engineering, innovation is the komodo dragon that drives progress and advancement. As we push the boundaries of what is possible, we encounter new challenges and opportunities, from the development of novel materials and devices to the creation of entirely new industries and applications. The 46 nanometer node, a milestone in the evolution of semiconductor manufacturing, represents a significant achievement in the pursuit of ever-smaller, ever-faster, and ever-more-efficient devices. And so, as we sit on the benches of knowledge, overlooking the vast expanse of human ingenuity, we are reminded of the profound impact that semiconductor engineering has had on our world. From the 🚬 symbol of smoking cessation to the 🏢 skyscrapers of modern cities, the influence of semiconductors is everywhere, a testament to the power of human creativity and innovation. As we gaze out upon the fault lines of progress, we are inspired to continue pushing the boundaries of what is possible, to explore the uncharted territories of science and technology, and to create a brighter, more wondrous future for all. In the stillness of the night, as the stars twinkle like diamonds in the sky, we are reminded of the magic of semiconductor engineering, a realm where the principles of physics and chemistry come together to create something truly remarkable. And as we drift off to sleep, our minds filled with visions of terbium and iridium, of rainbow-colored materials and disjointed patterns, we know that tomorrow will bring new wonders, new discoveries, and new innovations in the fascinating world of semiconductor engineering.

title: Petrology: Unveiling the Secrets of Rocks
text: Petrology: The Study of Rocks and Their Formation Petrology, a branch of geology, is the scientific study of rocks and their formation. It involves the analysis of the composition, texture, and structure of rocks to understand their origin, evolution, and properties. Petrologists use various techniques, including microscopy, geochemistry, and geophysics, to investigate the complex processes that shape our planet's crust. Types of Rocks Rocks can be broadly classified into three main categories: igneous, sedimentary, and metamorphic. Igneous rocks are formed from the cooling and solidification of magma or lava, while sedimentary rocks are created through the accumulation and compression of sediments. Metamorphic rocks, on the other hand, are formed when existing rocks are subjected to high temperatures and pressures, causing changes in their mineral composition and structure. Igneous Petrology Igneous petrology focuses on the study of igneous rocks, which can be further divided into intrusive and extrusive types. Intrusive rocks, such as granite, form beneath the Earth's surface, while extrusive rocks, like basalt, are produced by volcanic eruptions. The study of igneous rocks provides valuable insights into the Earth's thermal history, mantle dynamics, and the processes that shape our planet's surface. Sedimentary Petrology Sedimentary petrology examines the formation and characteristics of sedimentary rocks, which contain a wealth of information about the Earth's past environments, climates, and life forms. Sedimentary rocks can be composed of minerals, rock fragments, and organic matter, and their analysis can reveal details about ancient ecosystems, ocean chemistry, and the Earth's geological history. Metamorphic Petrology Metamorphic petrology investigates the transformations that occur in rocks under high pressure and temperature conditions, resulting in changes to their mineralogy, texture, and structure. Metamorphic rocks, such as marble and slate, provide clues about the Earth's tectonic evolution, mountain-building processes, and the movement of plates. Petrological Techniques Petrologists employ a range of techniques to analyze rocks, including optical microscopy, scanning electron microscopy, X-ray diffraction, and geochemical analysis. These methods allow researchers to determine the mineral composition, crystal structure, and chemical properties of rocks, providing a detailed understanding of their formation and evolution. Applications of Petrology Petrology has numerous practical applications in fields such as natural resource exploration, environmental monitoring, and geotechnical engineering. By understanding the properties and behavior of rocks, scientists can better predict and mitigate natural hazards, like earthquakes and landslides, and optimize the extraction of mineral resources. In conclusion, petrology is a fascinating field that offers a unique window into the Earth's history, composition, and dynamics. Through the study of rocks and their formation, petrologists can gain insights into the complex processes that shape our planet and inform strategies for sustainable resource management and environmental stewardship.

title: Agricultural Economics: The Backbone of Human Civilization
text: Agricultural Economics: The Backbone of Human Civilization Agricultural economics, a field that may seem mundane at first glance, is in fact a vibrant and complex discipline that underpins the very foundations of human society. It is the study of how agricultural resources are allocated, utilized, and managed to produce, distribute, and consume food and fiber products. The Importance of Agricultural Economics The significance of agricultural economics cannot be overstated. With the global population projected to reach 9.7 billion by 2050, the need for efficient and sustainable agricultural practices has never been more pressing. Agricultural economics plays a crucial role in addressing issues such as food security, poverty reduction, and environmental sustainability. Supply and Demand: The Invisible Hands of Agricultural Markets In agricultural economics, the concepts of supply and demand are fundamental in understanding market dynamics. The supply of agricultural products is influenced by factors such as weather conditions, technology, and government policies, while demand is driven by consumer preferences, population growth, and income levels. Mathematically, the supply and demand curves can be represented as: Supply curve: Qs = f(P, T, Tech, Gov) Demand curve: Qd = f(P, Pop, Inc) Where Qs and Qd are the quantities supplied and demanded, P is the price, T is technology, Tech is a vector of technological factors, Gov is government policy, Pop is population, and Inc is income. The Role of Technology in Agricultural Economics Technological advancements have revolutionized the agricultural sector, increasing productivity and efficiency. Precision agriculture, which involves the use of advanced technologies such as drones, satellite imaging, and machine learning algorithms, has enabled farmers to make data-driven decisions, reducing waste and improving crop yields. For instance, the use of precision agriculture can be represented by the Cobb-Douglas production function: Y = AK^αL^β Where Y is output, A is total factor productivity, K is capital, L is labor, and α and β are output elasticities. Agricultural Trade and Globalization International trade in agricultural products has become increasingly important, with countries specializing in the production and export of specific commodities. Agricultural trade is influenced by factors such as tariffs, quotas, and subsidies, which can have significant impacts on market outcomes. The gains from trade can be illustrated using the concept of comparative advantage, which states that countries should specialize in producing goods for which they have a lower opportunity cost. Mathematically, this can be represented as: Comparative advantage: OC_i / OC_j > 1 Where OC_i and OC_j are the opportunity costs of producing goods i and j, respectively. Conclusion In conclusion, agricultural economics is a vital field that underpins human civilization. Understanding the complex relationships between supply and demand, technology, trade, and globalization is essential for promoting sustainable agricultural practices, ensuring food security, and reducing poverty.

title: Bioarchaeology: Unveiling the Secrets of the Past
text: Bioarchaeology: A Journey Through Time Bioarchaeology, a subfield of archaeology, is an interdisciplinary approach that combines the study of human remains with archaeological context to reconstruct the lives of past societies. This fascinating field has revolutionized our understanding of human history, shedding light on the diet, health, and lifestyle of ancient cultures. As we delve into the world of bioarchaeology, we'll explore the intricacies of this science and uncover the secrets it holds. The Importance of Human Remains Human remains are a treasure trove of information, providing valuable insights into the biology, culture, and environment of past populations. Bioarchaeologists analyze skeletal remains to determine factors such as age, sex, stature, and ancestry. They also examine the presence of diseases, injuries, and other health conditions, which can reveal clues about the living conditions, diet, and lifestyle of ancient societies. For instance, the analysis of skeletal remains from ancient civilizations has shown that many people suffered from diseases such as tuberculosis, leprosy, and malaria, highlighting the significant impact of these diseases on human history. Diet and Nutrition Diet and nutrition play a crucial role in shaping human health, and bioarchaeology provides a unique window into the eating habits of past populations. By analyzing the stable isotopes of carbon, nitrogen, and oxygen in human bones and teeth, researchers can reconstruct the diet of ancient individuals. This information can be used to infer the types of food that were consumed, the level of dietary diversity, and even the presence of trade networks. For example, the analysis of isotopes in the bones of ancient Egyptians has revealed that they had a diet rich in fish and other aquatic resources, while the bones of ancient Inca warriors show a diet dominated by maize and other terrestrial plants. Health and Disease Bioarchaeology has greatly advanced our understanding of the evolution of human disease. The study of skeletal remains has provided evidence of the presence of diseases such as cancer, tuberculosis, and leprosy in ancient populations. Researchers have also identified the presence of infectious diseases such as plague, smallpox, and influenza, which have had a profound impact on human history. Furthermore, the analysis of ancient DNA has allowed scientists to track the spread of diseases across different regions and populations, providing valuable insights into the dynamics of disease transmission. Case Study: The Tasmanian Devil The tasmanian devil, an iconic animal native to Australia, has been the subject of extensive research in bioarchaeology. The study of tasmanian devil remains has provided valuable insights into the evolution of this unique species, including its diet, habitat, and behavior. For example, the analysis of tasmanian devil bones has revealed that they were apex predators, feeding on a variety of prey including wallabies, possums, and birds. This research has not only shed light on the biology of the tasmanian devil but also highlighted the importance of conservation efforts to protect this endangered species. As we conclude our journey through the world of bioarchaeology, we're reminded of the significance of this field in understanding human history and the natural world. By combining the study of human remains with archaeological context, bioarchaeologists have uncovered a wealth of information about the lives of past societies, from their diet and nutrition to their health and disease. As we continue to explore the secrets of the past, we're inspired by the possibilities that bioarchaeology holds for advancing our knowledge of the human experience 🛡 👫 🇺 ✪ 🇬.

text: Close Home Exclusives Recapitalization Financial Analysis Corporate Stories Interviews Investigations Metrics Nairalytics Economy Business News Budget Public Debt Tax Markets Currencies Cryptos Commodities Equities Fixed Income Funds Management Securities Sectors Agriculture Aviation Company News Consumer Goods Corporate Updates Corporate deals Corporate Press Releases Energy Entertainment Financial Services Health Hospitality & Travel Manufacturing Real Estate and Construction Renewables & Sustainability Tech News Financial Literacy Career tips Personal Finance Lifestyle Billionaire Watch Profiles Opinions Blurb Market Views Op-Eds Research Analysis Search Exclusives September 18, 2026 How much Nigerian fintechs could earn from Dangote Refinery’s N2.15 trillion IPO When the Dangote Petroleum Refinery IPO went live on the Nigerian Exchange on Monday, September 14, excitement among retail investors was enormous. Samuel Daniel Analyst 6 min read Follow Us on Google Discover When the Dangote Petroleum Refinery IPO went live on the Nigerian Exchange on Monday, September 14, excitement among retail investors was enormous. But that excitement was quickly followed by a problem for some of the digital platforms handling subscriptions. It was a crash. Within minutes, Bamboo posted on X that it was “getting much higher than expected traffic” and working to get the app “up and running” again. Cowrywise, another major digital investment platform, also reported difficulties as investors rushed to participate. Also Read Why Nigeria’s forex reserve is swelling Dangote IPO sparks record digital platform race for 10 million investors Why Lagos’ reclaimed land boom may not solve its housing problem This disruption offered an early glimpse of the scale of the subscription opportunity for fintechs and digital investment platforms distributing the offer. The money sitting behind the subscriptions Strip away the login failures and the rush by investors for the IPO points to something more important for these platforms: a potentially significant revenue opportunity tied to the value of subscriptions processed through their channels. Nairametrics spoke to Sycamore, a digital financial services company and one of the approved distribution channels for the Dangote Refinery IPO, to understand this. Sycamore said that fees for offers of this nature typically range from 50 to 100 basis points, or 0.5% to 1%, of subscription proceeds. In other words, the fee is linked to the amount of money investors subscribe through a distribution channel, rather than being a fixed charge per investor. Applied to the N2.15 trillion Dangote offer, that would imply between N10.75 billion and N21.5 billion in distribution fees could be shared across all the channels involved, if the same range applied across the full value of subscriptions. That does not mean fintechs will collectively receive that amount, or that any individual platform will earn a particular sum. Actual earnings would depend on the value of subscriptions processed through each channel, and the commercial terms agreed for the offer. Sycamore told Nairametrics that investors subscribing through its platform pay no charge. “Subscription done by investors through Sycamore is at no charge to the investor. However, we are eligible for a placement distribution fee on the IPO issue,” the company said. Sycamore said the fee is based on the value of subscription proceeds rather than the number of investors using its platform. “The fees receivable on the IPO distribution is based on the value of the subscription proceeds,” it said. It should not be treated as a confirmed industry-wide payout. Commercial terms can differ between intermediaries, while the amount any individual fintech earns would depend on the value of subscriptions processed through its channel. The fee is the smaller story But for the platforms, the direct distribution fee may not be the biggest commercial opportunity. Sycamore said it expects significant retail participation through its mobile app and web dashboard, with a target of between 500,000 and 1 million users. “We’ve designed a simplified subscription flow to make it very easy for anyone to start a subscription from scratch and complete it within minutes, ” the company said, adding that it had “optimized our platform to cater to these numbers comfortably.” “We believe the associated fees should adequately offset the technology investment and marketing/distribution expenses,” the company said. But the bigger opportunity, in Sycamore’s telling, is what happens after the subscription confirmation screen. “An IPO of this scale is far more than a one off fee event for us at Sycamore. It is one of the strongest retail investor acquisition events a fintech can get,” the company said. Sycamore said the long-term value of users acquired during a major IPO can outweigh the direct transaction fees because of the potential for cross-selling and deeper engagement. The platform also expects the offer to attract younger investors who are beginning to understand stocks, arguing that greater participation could help strengthen long-term investing habits and deepen activity in the Nigerian capital market. That makes the IPO commercially interesting to fintechs beyond the immediate distribution fee. A customer who joins a platform to subscribe for the Dangote IPO can potentially remain on the platform for other investments, trading products and financial services after the offer closes. For digital investment companies, the IPO is therefore both a transaction to process and an opportunity to acquire customers whose value could extend beyond the offering itself. What about tax?
